title: Modelling Framework for the Estimation of Salmonid Abundance
text: sample s (unique combination site visit, species lifestage) fished n_s passes, let y_{si} number fish caught pass p_{si} capture probability pass. probability fish first caught pass \pi_{si} = p_{si} \prod_{j < } (1 - p_{sj}) Conditional total catch, T_s = \sum_i y_{si}, counts multinomial probabilities \pi_{si} / P_s, P_s = \sum_i \pi_{si} cumulative capture probability. gives log likelihood \ell = \sum_s \left( \sum_i y_{si} \log \pi_{si} - T_s \log P_s \right) depend unknown number fish site. Capture probability modelled logit scale \text{logit}(p_{si}) = \mathbf{x}_{si}^\top \boldsymbol{\beta} + \mathbf{z}_{si}^\top \mathbf{b}, \qquad b_k \sim N(0, \sigma_{g(k)}^2) \boldsymbol{\beta} fixed effects \mathbf{b} optional random effects, example visit sample, one standard deviation \sigma_g random effect term. random effects integrated likelihood using Laplace approximation, fixed effects standard deviations estimated maximum likelihood using RTMB. Fish density estimated dividing total catch area fished cumulative capture probability: T_s / (A_s P_s).

title: Modelling Framework for the Estimation of Salmonid Abundance
text: Smooth terms penalised, amount smoothing estimated. smooth fitted random effect: part smooth penalised fixed effect, standard deviation random part controls smooth term . recommended smooths first second order random walks. use Markov random field (mrf) basis mgcv penalty created rw_penalty(). basis penalty sparse, models quick fit even walk many steps. first order random walk (order = 1) penalises differences neighbouring levels shrinks towards constant second order random walk (order = 2) penalises second differences shrinks towards linear trend covariate must factor whose levels steps walk, order. year factor replaced first order random walk years. standard deviation, sigma s(fyear), steps random walk logit scale. starting value walk fixed effect, intercept first year. smooth effect year capture probability, first pass fry Site1, approximate 95% confidence intervals  models year factor random walk years can compared using AIC random walk can steps data, example walk every day year sites fished . steps included penalty, factor given levels. second order random walk used day year (doy). case standard deviation close zero, smooth shrunk unpenalised part, linear trend day year (fixed effect s(fdoy).null1).  penalised smooth mgcv can used, example s(doy) te(doy, area), penalties sparse take longer fit. unpenalised regression spline, whose flexibility set basis dimension k, can fitted using fx = TRUE, example s(doy, k = 3, fx = TRUE).

Error ## sigma s(fyear)    0.192     0.1239 ##  ## Coefficients: ##               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z^2|) ## (Intercept)    0.59939     0.1565  3.8304  1.279e-04 ## siteIDSite2    0.08302     0.1345  0.6171  5.371e-01 ## siteIDSite3   -0.02424     0.1466 -0.1653  8.687e-01 ## pass122       -0.24364     0.1309 -1.8614  6.269e-02 ## lifestageParr  0.59448     0.1160  5.1239  2.993e-07 ##  ## Degrees of Freedom: 90 Total (i.e. Null);  84 Residual ## AIC: 3193 newdata <-   data.frame(     siteID = "Site1", pass12 = "1", lifestage = "Fry",     fyear = factor(levels(ef_data$fyear), levels = levels(ef_data$fyear))   ) pred <- predict(m1_smooth, newdata = newdata, se.fit = TRUE) year <- as.numeric(levels(ef_data$fyear))  plot(year, invlogit(pred$fit), type = "b", pch = 16, ylim = c(0, 1),      xlab = "Year", ylab = "Capture probability") lines(year, invlogit(pred$fit - 2 * pred$se.fit), lty = 2) lines(year, invlogit(pred$fit + 2 * pred$se.fit), lty = 2) AIC(m1, m1_smooth) ##           df      AIC ## m1         9 3188.305 ## m1_smooth  6 3192.599 days <- min(ef_data$doy):max(ef_data$doy) ef_data$fdoy <- factor(ef_data$doy, levels = days) rw2 <- rw_penalty(days, order = 2)  m1_doy <-   efp(     count ~ siteID + s(fdoy, bs = "mrf", xt = list(penalty = rw2)) +       pass12 + lifestage,     data = ef_data, pass = pass, id = sampleID   ) ##  ## Call: ## efp(formula = count ~ siteID + s(fdoy, bs = "mrf", xt = list(penalty = rw2)) +  ##     pass12 + lifestage, data = ef_data, pass = pass, id = sampleID) ##  ## Formula: ## count ~ siteID + s(fdoy, bs = "mrf", xt = list(penalty = rw2)) +  ##     pass12 + lifestage ##  ## Random effects: ##                Estimate Std. Error ## sigma s(fdoy) 3.937e-05   0.001866 ##  ## Coefficients: ##                Estimate Std. Error  z value Pr(>|z^2|) ## (Intercept)    0.678300     0.1178  5.75842  8.491e-09 ## siteIDSite2    0.001903     0.1448  0.01314  9.895e-01 ## siteIDSite3   -0.158737     0.1653 -0.96058  3.368e-01 ## pass122       -0.254290     0.1308 -1.94349  5.196e-02 ## lifestageParr  0.607910     0.1135  5.35677  8.472e-08 ## s(fdoy).null1 -0.550210     0.3837 -1.43391  1.516e-01 ##  ## Degrees of Freedom: 90 Total (i.e. Null);  83 Residual ## AIC: 3196 newdata <-   data.frame(     siteID = "Site1", pass12 = "1", lifestage = "Fry",     fdoy = factor(days, levels = days)   ) pred <- predict(m1_doy, newdata = newdata, se.fit = TRUE)  plot(days, invlogit(pred$fit), type = "l", ylim = c(0, 1),      xlab = "Day of year", ylab = "Capture probability") lines(days, invlogit(pred$fit - 2 * pred$se.fit), lty = 2) lines(days, invlogit(pred$fit + 2 * pred$se.fit), lty = 2) rug(ef_data$doy)

title: Modelling Framework for the Estimation of Salmonid Abundance
text: Aggregate counts sampleID (.e. counts fry parr per site visit) Reshape get capture probability species x lifestage x site visit x pass. facilitates summary P. Get cumulative capture probability sampleID (see Glover et al., 2018) Remove individual pass capture probabilities Remove pass pass-specific data dataframe Join data cumulative counts sampleID Join data cumulative capture probability sampleID
code: counts <- aggregate(count ~ sampleID, ef_data, sum) probs <- cast(ef_data, formula = sampleID ~ pass, value = "prob") probs $ prob <- apply(probs[,2:4], 1, function(x) 1 - prod(1-x)) probs <- select(probs, sampleID, prob) densdata <- unique(select(ef_data, -count, -prob, -pass, -pass12)) densdata <- left_join(densdata, counts, by = "sampleID") densdata <- left_join(densdata, probs, by = "sampleID")

title: Modelling Framework for the Estimation of Salmonid Abundance
text: Density (N/m-2) estimated \frac{counts}{area*P} want model counts directly (Poisson model), need cumulative P area offset. Poisson model offset \log({area*cumulativeP}). Plot check
code: densdata $ Density_Estimate <- densdata $ count / (densdata $ area *                                                       densdata $ prob) densdata $ offset <- log(densdata $ area * densdata $ prob)
